claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 9110 §3.3 (line 768): "HTTP is defined as a stateless protocol, meaning that each request message's semantics can be understood in isolation, and that the relationship between connections and messages on them has no impact on the interpretation of those messages."

RFC 9110 §3.3 (line 778): "a server MUST NOT assume that two requests on the same connection are from the same user agent unless the connection is secured and specific to that agent." RFC 9112 §9.3: persistent connections carry several requests. Current §4 text "One TCP connection can carry several requests one after another, but it only moves bytes" matches. Live 2026-09-27 06:44: one curl -v with two /admin URLs prints "Reusing existing http: connection with host localhost".
claim_verdicts.source: refs/rfc/rfc9112.txt; refs/rfc/rfc9110.txt; live curl -v in donhang-lab

claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 6265 §3 (line 300): "In subsequent requests, the user agent returns a Cookie request header to the origin server. The Cookie header contains cookies the user agent received in previous Set-Cookie headers." Live run step 2 prints the Set-Cookie line; step 4 with -b gets 200.

RFC 6265 §4.1.1 (line 456): set-cookie-string = cookie-pair *( ";" SP cookie-av ) - one pair per Set-Cookie. §4.2.1 (line 701): cookie-string = cookie-pair *( ";" SP cookie-pair ) - several pairs on one Cookie line.

RFC 6265 §5.4: the user agent includes stored cookies in the Cookie header; cookie-list = cookies whose host-only domain equals the request-host (or domain-matches it), whose path path-matches and whose secure-only-flag is met; no Domain attribute sets host-only-flag (§5.3). Live: the curl run with -b sends sid and /admin answers 200, request otherwise unchanged.

RFC 6265 §4.1.2.4 (line 643): "The user agent will include the cookie in an HTTP request only if the path portion of the request-uri matches (or is a subdirectory of) the cookie's Path attribute" - every path is under "/".

RFC 6265 §4.1.2.6 (lines 681-684): "the attribute instructs the user agent to omit the cookie when providing access to cookies via \"non-HTTP\" APIs (such as a web browser API that exposes cookies to scripts)."

RFC 6265 §4.1.2.5 (line 657): cookie sent "only if the request is transmitted over a secure channel (typically HTTP over Transport Layer Security (TLS))". §8.3 (line 1665): "Unless sent over a secure channel (such as TLS), the information in the Cookie and Set-Cookie headers is transmitted in the clear." §4.1.2.6: HttpOnly "is independent of the Secure attribute".

grep -ci samesite refs/rfc/*.txt -> 0 in rfc6265, 9110, 9111, 9112 (re-checked 2026-09-27). SameSite is defined in RFC 6265bis, not mirrored in refs/ and not a docs root in content/versions.yaml. Kind behavior, so not a D1 blocker. Live run only shows the lab sets SameSite=Lax, not what it restricts.

RFC 6265 §8.4 (lines 1716-1725): "servers commonly store a nonce (or \"session identifier\") in a cookie. When the server receives an HTTP request with a nonce, the server can look up state information associated with the cookie using the nonce as a key." and "the nonce is useful only for interacting with the server".

Caddyfile@stage-0 (ff911b0): ":8080 {" plain HTTP; handle /login.html { header Set-Cookie "sid=dev-session-1; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax" file_server }. No Secure. Re-run 2026-09-27 step 2 prints exactly that line.
